patterns_found.visual_evidence: The desktop sketch shows a persistent full-width top header bar spanning the page, visually separated from the scrolling content below, which strongly implies a fixed or sticky navigation/header region.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: Header should remain visible while scrolling and preserve access to branding and top-level navigation/actions.
patterns_found.ambiguities: It is unclear whether only the top bar is sticky or whether any secondary navigation within the content area also remains fixed.

sketch_notes: These sketches mostly depict long-form documentation/article layouts with images, tables, and text blocks rather than explicit interactive widgets. The only clearly implied JavaScript behavior from the drawings themselves is a sticky desktop header/navigation bar. The mobile sketch appears to be a straightforward scrolling article without visible menu, search, accordion, tabs, modal triggers, or load-more affordances. Cross-viewport differences therefore seem minimal in the sketch evidence, aside from the desktop header being visually prominent enough to suggest sticky behavior.
